author: cilcisme
title: Love the game, but the bugs and monetization are getting really frustrating.
content:
I have been a fan of this game for years, but the bugs are getting really frustrating, especially when they hinder competitive play, cost diamonds, lost rewards, not to mention the rewards one doesn’t receive after they’ve been payed for with letters! And it’s so frustrating not receiving a letter for every help provided. A max of 7 per day is sooo frustrating, especially when I help 30 people one day, and only one or two the next!!! There is absolutely no reason they should be limited! Help might be more consistent if there was more of a benefit to the help. 
One great thing about the game is the evolution. That being said, before rolling out new features, it would be so nice if the development team did a better job of testing functionality. I love having the opportunity to reactivate a derby task when it expires, but when the harvesting resumes and isn’t counted, it’s more frustrating than having the task expire in the first place!!! 
And your bot support is so very frustrating! I really miss the human support of days past. We never receive feedback when a bug is fixed, and we receive nothing, not even an apology, in response to the inconvenience of the ever increasing bugs! I don’t know how many times I’ve reported a bug, the bot asks questions or makes suggestions, and then after I respond to the bots suggestions, I’m informed that the bug is a known issue. If it’s a known issue, why not just tell me that in the first place, rather than wasting my time with frustrating, needless dialogue?!
I truly love all of the new decor you’re continually creating. It’s truly wonderful and probably one of the only reasons I continue playing. But it’s very frustrating that so much of it is unattainable unless one pays an exorbitant amount of real money for it. Do you not realize how much the cost of real living has increased? Your game is very, very lucrative. As is your greed.
You’re one of the top games in the world. Do better.

author: thisisourland
title: Love the game, hate the pay to progress.
content:
I absolutely love Hay Day! It’s fun, relaxing, and honestly one of the few mobile games I’ve really enjoyed sticking with. However, there are a few things that are becoming incredibly frustrating and take away from the experience.

1. Upgrade and expansion materials are WAY too difficult to get.
Between expanding land and upgrading the barn and silo, you need so many materials, yet actually finding them is nearly impossible. Trying to buy them through the newspaper is basically a race, you click on something the second you see it and it’s already sold. Progress shouldn’t depend so heavily on getting lucky or being faster than every other player.

There really needs to be a better and FAIRER way to earn or purchase larger quantities of necessary materials through gameplay. Give us more opportunities through crops, animals, orders, events, achievements, or even a shop with reasonable limits.

2. The game feels increasingly pay-to-progress.
Diamonds are needed for so many things, especially opening additional production slots, and then there are decorations that can only be purchased with diamonds. Of course I understand a free game needs optional purchases, but there should be a better balance between spending real money and simply playing the game.

Players shouldn’t feel like they have to continuously buy diamonds just to comfortably grow their farm, expand production, and progress at a reasonable pace.

I genuinely LOVE this game, which is exactly why these things are so disappointing. Please give players more ways to earn upgrade/expansion materials and diamonds through actual gameplay instead of making everything feel like a race or another purchase.

Hay Day has so much going for it. It just needs a better balance between fun, progression, and monetization. Please listen to your players and make progression feel rewarding again…. not frustrating or expensive!

author: ConcernedmotheR5589
title: Great Game! With one update suggestion!
content:
I’ve been playing Hay Day on and off for the last 8 years, and as a level 58 player, I can honestly say it’s one of my favorite mobile games. The graphics are charming, the gameplay is relaxing, and there’s always something to work toward. It’s one of the few games I keep coming back to year after year.

The only thing I’d really love to see changed is the daily purchasing limit on expansion materials. Right now, you can only buy 80 expansion materials every 24 hours, regardless of what type they are. While that makes sense for common items like screws, nails, planks, tape, and wood panels—since players buy those constantly to upgrade their barns and silos—it becomes frustrating when it comes to land expansion materials.

Items like marker stakes, mallets, and land deeds are incredibly rare to find because almost nobody sells them. It honestly feels like you have maybe a 15% chance of finding someone willing to sell them, if that. Since they’re so difficult to come across, they really shouldn’t count toward the same purchase limit as the common barn and silo materials.

I think a great quality-of-life improvement would be to have separate purchase limits: one for barn and silo upgrade materials, and another for land expansion materials. It would make expanding your farm feel much more balanced without making the game too easy.

Overall, I absolutely love Hay Day and will continue playing. This is just one suggestion that I think would make an already great game even better in a future update!

author: Atefex
title: Long-Time Player Feedback: Hay Day Needs Better Progression
content:
I’ve been playing Supercell games for around 7–8 years. I actively play Hay Day, Clash of Clans, Clash Royale, and Brawl Stars, and I’ve always considered myself a loyal fan of your games. That’s exactly why I’m writing this feedback.

The biggest problem with Hay Day is that progression eventually becomes unnecessarily difficult. Expanding land and buying new production machines takes an unreasonable amount of time and coins. Right now, I still have several machines that I simply can’t afford because earning enough coins has become incredibly slow.

Hay Day is supposed to be a relaxing game. I play it to unwind after a long day, not to feel stressed. Unfortunately, the current economy does the exact opposite. Instead of feeling rewarded for my time, I often feel like I’m constantly falling behind.

Another major issue is the newspaper and shop system. Most of the listings are filled with items that almost nobody needs, while useful materials appear so rarely that they’re sold out before you can even open the seller’s shop. The loading time between tapping an advertisement and entering the farm makes this even more frustrating. Countless times I’ve found the exact item I needed, only to see “Sold Out” before I even had a chance to buy it.

This isn’t exciting gameplay—it’s simply frustrating.

I genuinely love Hay Day, and that’s why this is disappointing. I don’t want to quit the game after investing years into it, but there are moments when I honestly think deleting it would be less stressful than continuing to play.

Please consider making progression feel more rewarding, improving the in-game economy, and redesigning the newspaper system so players have a fair chance to purchase the items they actually need. Hay Day has always been one of the most relaxing farming games, and I hope it can feel that way again.

author: ……(unknown)……
title: BEST GAME EVER, read the whole thing, I mean it, read it all!!!
content:
I’ve had this game all my life and this is so much fun. It’s everything a person could ask for. Read the whole thing if you want to learn everything about this game. I mean everything about this game.

You get to farm and do all the jobs real farmers do! You get to plant and harvest crops, feed your animals, get what people eat from animals like milk from cows and goats, wool from sheep, and bacon from pigs. You also get to have your own barn and silo! You also can have fruit plants like apple trees and blackberry bushes! You get fruit from them. 

You get to have all these machines and make things to sell using the stuff you farmed! You have to fill the machines and get things you need to fill them and they make things! 

You know how farmers sell their crops? Well you also get to! There’s this truck that you fill with things you have and send them off and get money! 

The boat is very similar to the truck, you get what you need to fill it and put all the orders in their slots. The time limit to fill the boat is the whole day so you’ve got plenty of time before it’s shipped off and you get your reward. If you fill the whole ship, you get a huge reward!

Next, you have a stand that you put your items on and people buy them. You get to choose which items, how many of the items, and the price of them! This gets you plenty of money.

The newspaper is a place where you can visit other people’s farms and buy what they have for sale in their stand I just talked about. You can get things you need here. 

You get to have so many animals! Animals real farmers have including cows, goats, pigs, sheep, bees, rabbits, horses, peacocks, and more! So many animals. 

Oh my goodness this part is fun. You get to dress up your animals in cute outfits! It’s so fun to see them. 

The animals are like real animals, they eat and sleep. You have to make their food using crops. 

You get to have friends and choose your farm name! You can visit their farms and buy their items for sale. 

Greg’s farm is so great! You can explore it all day. Also, his things for sale? He puts new things for sale every day for such cheap prices!!! So cheap! That helps a lot. 

Now, the town. The town is a place where you can go and sell things to people. They pay you good money and work at all these fun stores! 

Fishing. When you go fishing, you can catch all these fish. You keep track of all the fish you’ve caught. You make fish bait or the rods and pick a part to fish. You get to fish on your own. You find a fish under the water and grab hold of it. It tries to swim away so you must pull it and keep it there until you can get the fish. 

Helping people. As you visit each other’s farms you might see a help sign. You place help signs in places you need help in, that can be with dead plants like trees and bushes of fruit, things you need to fill the boat or truck, and more.

You get to buy more land so you can put more things like more animals and places for crops to grow and machinery. Also there are so many cute little accessories to add to your farm. You do have to purchase them though. 

Ready for a great part? YOU DON’T KILL THE ANIMALS!!! When you get bacon from pigs you don’t kill them! They stay there and don’t die! They don’t even die from age! So once you buy an animal, you have it forever. Such a great part. 

Here’s my singular complaint about this game: prices. The prices of things are too high! I wish things costed less. I have to pay so much for things. I’m already broke! Well, I’ve been trying to get this singular horse for so long but I can’t because of costs too much. 

Great game, best one ever. Love it. 100/10.

author: Jean-Claude Van Damme effed ur
title: Happy 14th Birthday, Hay Day!
content:
Happy 14th Birthday, Hay Day!

Coming into Hay Day, I was definitely the target audience. I have thousands of hours across Supercell games, especially Clash of Clans, and I was also a top 1% player worldwide in Beatstar before Supercell shut it down. Because of that, I’ve spent a lot of time with games that require long-term progression, resource management, and daily play. 

Overall, I genuinely enjoy the game. It’s very polished, easy to understand, and probably one of the most user-friendly mobile games I’ve played. The art style is charming, the controls are simple, and there always seems to be something to do. Expanding your farm, producing goods, filling orders, and trading with other players is surprisingly relaxing and satisfying. It has that same “I’ll just check in for five minutes” feeling that turns into an hour.

That said, I do have some issues with the game’s economy and pacing.

Gems are incredibly expensive for what they provide, and it’s surprisingly easy to burn through them in seconds. At the same time, the game doesn’t reward players with many free gems, so using them often feels punishing instead of exciting. Cooking and production times for many items can also become excessive, especially when several machines are tied up for hours at a time. Waiting long periods for basic ingredients, needing multiple products to make a single item, limited machine slots, and other small time gates can make progression feel more taxing than rewarding.

I completely understand that free-to-play games need monetization, but Hay Day sometimes feels a little too eager to push players toward spending money to avoid waiting. I’d love to see more opportunities to earn gems naturally and perhaps some reductions to production times on higher-level items.

Even with those criticisms, Hay Day is still a very enjoyable game and one of the better farming simulators on mobile. It’s relaxing, well-designed, and easy to recommend to anyone looking for a casual game they can play for months or even years. Happy 14th anniversary, and here’s to many more years of farming.
